findings.title: Vulnerable runtime transitive dependency @grpc/grpc-js 1.14.4 with a non-blocking audit gate
evidence: apps/realtime/package.json:22 "@opentelemetry/sdk-node": "0.222.0" (production dep pulls the gRPC exporters)
findings.impact: CVE-2026-101916 (high, getAuthContext authorization confusion) and CVE-2026-101915 (low) ship in the runtime image; both fixed in 1.14.5/1.13.6, but CI treats npm audit as advisory so the vulnerable version can reach production.
findings.recommendation: Bump @grpc/grpc-js to 1.14.5 (overrides or lockfile refresh), then make the high-severity audit step blocking in both workflows.

findings.title: GitHub Action upload-artifact@v4 not pinned to a commit SHA
findings.impact: A mutable major tag can be repointed upstream and execute arbitrary code in CI with the repository read token.
findings.recommendation: Pin line 55 to the same ea165f8d... SHA and add a guard/Dependabot rule preventing tag refs.

findings.title: Container base and CI service images not pinned by digest
findings.impact: Mutable base/service tags break reproducibility and are a tag-repointing supply-chain vector; the app images are less hardened than the ancillary compose images.
findings.recommendation: Pin every node: and postgres: reference by @sha256 digest, or document a periodic digest-refresh step.

findings.title: Supply-chain license/vulnerability workflow is not a required branch-protection check
evidence: .github/workflows/supply-chain.yml:1-7 states these are merge-gating supply-chain checks
findings.impact: License allow-list and production audit results do not block merges to main, contradicting the workflow's stated purpose; the policy validator cannot detect the drift.
findings.recommendation: Add license-and-vulnerability to requiredStatusChecks.contexts and extend verify-branch-protection.mjs to enumerate all workflow files.

findings.title: Six tracked shell scripts lack the executable bit
evidence: scripts/ci-db-tests.sh, scripts/ci-migrations-dryrun.sh, scripts/install-clean.sh, scripts/migrations-manifest.sh, scripts/repo-secret-scan.sh, scripts/verify-all.sh (git ls-files -s mode 100644)
findings.impact: Low: ./script.sh fails on POSIX, but every documented invocation uses an explicit bash interpreter.
findings.recommendation: git update-index --chmod=+x on the six files for consistency.

findings.title: Secret scan allowlists whole files, masking future real secrets
findings.impact: All 16 generic-api-key hits are benign fixtures, but path-level allowlisting means a real credential later appended to those files bypasses CI detection.
findings.recommendation: Replace whole-file allowlists with rule/regex-scoped allowlists and periodically re-scan allowlisted files.

findings.title: Metrics token compared non-constant-time and has no rotation path
evidence: apps/realtime/src/server.ts:2011 if (configured && token === configured) return true;
findings.impact: Static never-rotated ops credential; non-constant-time comparison is a low network timing-side-channel.
findings.recommendation: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers and document METRICS_TOKEN rotation in the secret rotation runbook.

findings.title: Empty service-role key silently disables persistence; no committed rotation evidence
evidence: apps/realtime/src/services/supabase.ts:39-44 if (!key) { ... return null; } disables trusted run persistence
docs/archive/agent_final_response.json:695 "R-021 OPEN_PENDING_ROTATION: owner-side .env plaintext credentials - rotation is an owner action"
findings.impact: A misconfigured production deploy can run without trusted persistence/scoring instead of failing closed; rotation is unverifiable from the repository.
findings.recommendation: Fail boot/readiness when NODE_ENV=production and the service-role key is empty; commit a dated rotation runbook.

findings.title: CODEOWNERS is a personal account; release/hotfix branch rules absent
evidence: .github/CODEOWNERS:5 * @MaineCyberTech (comment: personal account, not an org team)
findings.impact: Required CODEOWNERS review resolves to a single personal account (bus-factor / merge-authority ambiguity); release and hotfix branches are not covered by the declared policy; live policy is unverifiable from the repo without a token.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an organization team handle and add a release/hotfix ruleset to the declared policy.

findings.title: Residual CRLF files and hadolint DL3025 HEALTHCHECK warnings
evidence: git ls-files --eol at d79d0d7: i/crlf only for docs/archive/reviewer.md and evidence/phase2/20260908T2110Z-p2/G16-supply-chain/g16_finding_disposition_ledger.csv
apps/web/Dockerfile:50, apps/realtime/Dockerfile:49, Dockerfile.p2runtime:11 hadolint DL3025 (HEALTHCHECK shell-form CMD)
findings.impact: Cosmetic: the deterministic '21 CRLF files' claim is not reproducible at HEAD; hadolint only flags HEALTHCHECK lines, while real CMD lines are already JSON.
findings.recommendation: git add --renormalize the two files; optionally convert HEALTHCHECK to JSON array form.
